The root of the word emphasizes a marked distinction between loyalties, where commitment to Christ can lead to tensions within family relationships. Theologically, this reminds us that following Christ sometimes requires making difficult choices that can distance us from those we love.

This term means 'father' and refers to the patriarchal figure in the family. In Jewish culture, the father holds a central and authoritative position. The use of this word in this verse underscores the importance of family relationships while indicating that loyalty to God can sometimes conflict with familial expectations. Spiritually, this challenges us regarding our faithfulness to God above earthly ties.

This word means 'mother' and represents a figure of tenderness and protection in the family. In the context of Matthew 10:35, it emphasizes that even the closest relationships can be tested by faith. This reminds us that faith in Christ can require sacrifices, even in the most cherished relationships. Theologically, this prompts us to reflect on the primacy of our commitment to God.

This term means 'daughter-in-law' and evokes relationships through marriage. In the cultural context, the relationships between daughters-in-law and mothers-in-law can be complex. The inclusion of this word in the verse underscores that even bonds created by marriage are not exempt from tensions when faith is involved. This teaches us that our commitment to Christ transcends even familial alliances.

35.epoque: This passage was written in a context where family relationships were of great importance in first-century Jewish society. Family ties were often considered sacred and indissoluble.
35.passage: In Matthew 10, Jesus sends His disciples to preach the Gospel and warns them of the challenges they will encounter. This verse emphasizes that the message of the Gospel can provoke divisions even within families, as it calls for a supreme loyalty to God.
35.culture: In Jewish culture, family honor and intergenerational relationships are paramount. Separation from a family member due to faith was a shocking event, highlighting the cost of discipleship.
35.interpretation: This verse reminds us that following Jesus can lead to conflicts in our closest relationships. It emphasizes that our commitment to Christ must take precedence over our family loyalties, which can be a painful but necessary trial in our spiritual journey.
35.commentaire: This passage calls us to reflect on our spiritual priorities. As disciples, we must be prepared to face divisions to remain faithful to our calling. It encourages us to put our faith first, even when it involves sacrifices in our personal relationships.

mots.sens: This term refers to enemies or adversaries. In the biblical context, it evokes not only physical opposition but also spiritual hostility. The root of the word underscores the idea of separation due to conflicts, which is particularly relevant here, as it indicates that even those who are close can become opponents because of faith. This highlights the reality of tensions that can arise in family relationships due to commitment to Christ.

This word means 'house' or 'home', and it represents not only a physical place but also the notion of family and community. In Jewish culture, the home is the center of social and spiritual life. By mentioning the house, the verse emphasizes that conflicts can arise not only outside but also within the most intimate relationships, which is a call to recognize the depth of spiritual choices.

36.epoque: In Jesus' time, the Jewish people lived under Roman occupation and faced religious and social tensions. Jewish beliefs and practices often conflicted with the new ideas brought by Christ, creating divisions within families and communities.
36.passage: In Matthew 10, Jesus sends His disciples to preach the Gospel and warns them of the persecutions they will encounter. This chapter addresses the challenges believers must face, including division within families, due to their commitment to Him.
36.culture: In Jewish culture, family is of paramount importance, and being at odds with family members was a sensitive issue. Allegiance to God could lead to ruptures in family relationships, which was particularly difficult in a context where family honor was valued.
36.interpretation: This verse reminds us that following Christ can lead to conflicts, even with those who are closest to us. It highlights the reality that faith can provoke divisions, as it sometimes requires choices that are not understood or accepted by others, including family.
36.commentaire: This passage encourages us to be aware of the sacrifices that our faith may demand. Even if it can lead to tensions, it is essential to remain steadfast in our commitment to Christ. It reminds us that our true family is the one that shares the faith, and we must pray for those who do not understand our choice, while remaining faithful to our calling.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to love' in a deep and selfless sense. It evokes an affection that goes beyond mere feelings, involving total commitment and devotion. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that love for God must surpass all other affections, including those for family members, revealing the absolute priority that God must have in the believer's life.

This term means 'worthy' or 'valuable'. In the context of this verse, it indicates that a person's worth as a disciple of Christ is measured by their ability to place God above all other loves. This highlights the radical demand of the Christian faith, where the disciple is called to renounce any loyalty that might rival their commitment to Christ.

This word means 'father' and represents not only the paternal figure in the family but also the source of authority and protection. In Jewish culture, love and respect for parents are fundamental. However, this verse emphasizes that even this sacred relationship must be subordinated to love for Christ, highlighting the radical nature of the Christian faith.

This term designates a 'child' or 'son'. It evokes the intimate and affectionate relationship between parents and children. However, Jesus teaches here that even this natural love must be relativized in relation to love for Him, thus underscoring the importance of prioritizing our relationship with God above familial ties.

37.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' ministry in the 1st century, where family relationships were considered fundamental in Jewish society.
37.passage: In Matthew 10, Jesus sends His disciples on a mission, teaching them the realities of discipleship and the sacrifices they will have to make. This verse emphasizes the demand for loyalty to Christ, even at the expense of family relationships.
37.culture: In Jewish culture, honor and respect for family are paramount. However, Jesus challenges these norms by asserting that commitment to God must take precedence over all other loyalties.
37.interpretation: This verse reminds us that the Christian faith demands a radical priority of love for Christ. This does not mean we should neglect our families, but rather that our relationship with God must be at the center of our lives, influencing all our other relationships.
37.commentaire: This passage invites us to reflect on our priorities. Being worthy of Christ involves placing our love for Him above all, including our most cherished relationships. It calls us to evaluate our commitments and ensure that our devotion to God illuminates all our interactions and decisions.

mots.sens: The word 'σταυρός' denotes a 'cross', a symbol of suffering and death, but also of sacrifice and redemption. In the biblical context, it evokes the idea of bearing the weight of one's own trials and submitting to God's will. Spiritually, this underscores the importance of self-denial in following Christ, who Himself bore His cross for our salvation.

The term 'ἀκολουθέω' means 'to follow' and implies a voluntary and deliberate action of walking in someone's footsteps. In the context of the Christian faith, this means not only following Jesus' teachings but also imitating His example of life. This highlights the total commitment that each disciple must have towards Christ.

The word 'ἄξιος' means 'worthy' and expresses a value or merit. In this verse, it emphasizes that a disciple's worth is linked to their ability to take up their cross and follow Jesus. This implies a spiritual evaluation of our commitment and faithfulness to Christ.

38.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' earthly ministry in the first century, where He preached and taught in Israel, facing religious and political opposition.
38.passage: In Matthew 10, Jesus sends His disciples on a mission, giving them instructions on how to preach the Gospel. He prepares them to face persecutions and urges them to be ready to renounce everything to follow Him.
38.culture: The cross was an instrument of torture and execution in Roman culture, symbolizing shame and suffering. For early Christians, bearing one's cross was a call to identify with Christ and to suffer for the faith.
38.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true disciple of Christ must be ready to sacrifice their own desires and comforts to follow Him. The cross represents the struggles and sacrifices necessary to live a life in accordance with Jesus' call.
38.commentaire: Taking up one's cross is a call to a life of authentic discipleship, where we must be willing to renounce our own interests to serve Christ. It reminds us that the path of faith is not always easy, but it is essential to be worthy of our Lord. As believers, we are called to embrace our challenges in faith, knowing that our commitment to Christ brings us closer to Him.

mots.sens: This term means 'life' in the broadest sense, encompassing not only physical existence but also spiritual and eternal life. In the biblical context, it refers to the life that God gives, which is full and abundant. The nuance here is that life in Christ transcends mere earthly survival, highlighting the depth of communion with God.

This verb means 'to lose' or 'to destroy', implying a loss that can be definitive. In the context of this verse, it evokes the notion of renouncing one's own life or selfish desires to embrace a higher calling. The theological significance here is that true life is not found in self-preservation but in submission to Christ.

This preposition means 'for the sake of' or 'for the benefit of', indicating a motivation or purpose. In this verse, it emphasizes that the loss of life must be intentional and directed towards a greater cause, that of Christ. This reminds us that our commitment to God must be a priority and that our sacrifice has eternal value.

39.epoque: In the first century, the Christian community faced increasing persecution, and Jesus' disciples were called to renounce their former lives to follow a path of suffering and sacrifice.
39.passage: In Matthew 10, Jesus sends His disciples to preach the Gospel, preparing them for opposition and persecution. This verse summarizes the essence of the call to discipleship, where faithfulness to Christ requires self-denial.
39.culture: In the Jewish and Roman culture of the time, life was often valued by status and possessions. Jesus overturns this conception by teaching that true value lies in the relationship with God and the mission He entrusts.
39.interpretation: This verse teaches us that true life can only be found by renouncing our own selfish desires and fully dedicating ourselves to Christ. The promise of finding life is an encouragement for those who choose to follow Jesus, even at the cost of personal sacrifices.
39.commentaire: Matthew 10:39 reminds us that the path of faith is often marked by renunciations. By choosing to lose our life for Christ, we discover a life full of meaning and abundance. This verse invites us to evaluate our priorities and embrace sacrifice as a means of entering into the fullness of life that God has for us.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to welcome' or 'to receive.' In the biblical context, it implies not only a physical acceptance but also a spiritual recognition of the authority of the one being received. This emphasizes the importance of hospitality and welcoming God's messengers as acts of faith that unite believers with the divine mission.

This word means 'to send' and is the root of the term 'apostle.' It evokes the idea of mission and divine authority. In this verse, it emphasizes that whoever receives the messenger of Christ also receives God's authority and mission, reinforcing the responsibility of believers to welcome those who bear the divine word.

This personal pronoun means 'I' and is used by Jesus to affirm His divine identity. In this context, it highlights the direct connection between Jesus, the Father, and His disciples. This reinforces the idea that welcoming the disciples is an act of recognition of Christ's own authority.

This term designates a 'prophet,' a person chosen by God to convey His word. In the verse, it reminds us that those who welcome God's messengers participate in the prophetic mission, thereby receiving the blessing and authority that come with it.

40.epoque: This verse is set in the context of Jesus' ministry in the 1st century, where He sends His disciples to preach the Gospel to the Jews. It is a time of religious and political tensions in Israel, marked by messianic expectation.
40.passage: Matthew 10 deals with the sending of the twelve disciples, where Jesus gives them specific instructions for their mission. This passage emphasizes the importance of their role as representatives of Christ and how they should be welcomed by the community.
40.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, hospitality was a fundamental value. Welcoming a messenger of God was seen as an act of faith and obedience, strengthening communal and spiritual bonds.
40.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that welcoming the disciples is, in reality, welcoming Jesus Himself, and therefore, God the Father. This highlights the importance of communion among believers and the responsibility to welcome God's word into their lives.
40.commentaire: This passage reminds us that every act of welcome and support towards God's messengers is significant. As believers, we are called to recognize and honor those who bear the Gospel, for in receiving them, we also receive the presence and authority of Christ. This encourages us to be open and receptive to God's word in our daily lives.

mots.sens: The word 'prophet' designates a spokesperson for God, someone who communicates divine will. In the biblical context, a prophet is often tasked with delivering messages of rebuke, encouragement, or revelation. Spiritually, receiving a prophet involves welcoming God's word and recognizing His authority, which paves the way for divine blessing.

The term 'just' refers to a person who is in accordance with God's will, acting with justice and integrity. It can also evoke a state of correct relationship with God, based on faith. In this verse, welcoming a just person means recognizing and honoring those who live according to divine principles, which is essential for an authentic Christian life.

41.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' earthly ministry in the 1st century, where He sent His disciples to preach the Gospel and prepare the way for His kingdom. Prophets and the just were respected figures in Jewish society, often in opposition to established religious authorities.
41.passage: Matthew 10 deals with the sending of the disciples on mission, where Jesus gives them instructions on how to preach and act. This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and welcoming God's messengers, as well as the spiritual consequences of these actions.
41.culture: In Jewish culture, hospitality and welcoming prophets and the just were fundamental values. Welcoming a prophet or a just person was seen as a way to participate in their ministry and receive the blessings that followed.
41.interpretation: This verse teaches that the way we welcome God's servants has spiritual repercussions on our own lives. Receiving a prophet or a just person as such means recognizing their role and mission, which allows us to benefit from the spiritual rewards associated with it.
41.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of welcoming and recognizing God's servants in our lives. By honoring those who preach the truth and live according to justice, we place ourselves under the influence of their ministry and receive the blessings that follow. Let us be attentive to how we welcome God's messengers, as this can transform our relationship with Him and enrich our spiritual life.

mots.sens: This word means 'small' or 'little.' It can refer to children, people of little social importance, or symbolically, those who are humble in faith. In this verse, it underscores the importance of every disciple of Christ, regardless of their status or spiritual stature, and reminds us that each one deserves to be treated with dignity and respect.

This term means 'gift' or 'offering.' It evokes the idea of giving without expecting anything in return, an act of generosity. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that even the smallest act of kindness, like giving a cup of water, is precious in God's eyes and holds eternal value.

This word means 'disciple' or 'student.' It designates those who follow a master to learn from him. In the context of this verse, it reminds us that Christ's disciples are called to live in community and to be supported by others, highlighting the importance of mutual aid in faith.

This term means 'reward' or 'return.' It evokes the idea of receiving back what one has given. Spiritually, it reminds us that God sees and rewards even the smallest acts of kindness, affirming that everything we do for others in His name has eternal value.

42.epoque: In Jesus' time, society was stratified, and disciples faced both social and spiritual challenges in following a controversial master. Small acts of kindness were often overlooked in a world where social status prevailed.
42.passage: In Matthew 10, Jesus sends His disciples to preach and prepares them for persecution. This verse emphasizes the importance of acts of service, even the most modest, in the context of their mission.
42.culture: In Jewish culture, hospitality and service were fundamental values. Offering water to a traveler was an act of kindness and respect, and it took on a deeper spiritual significance in the context of serving God.
42.interpretation: This verse teaches that every act, no matter how small, done for a disciple of Christ is significant and will be rewarded by God. It underscores the importance of generosity and love within the Christian community.
42.commentaire: This passage reminds us that our service to God is not measured by the greatness of our actions but by the sincerity of our hearts. Even the simplest gestures, like giving a cup of water, can have an eternal impact. Let us be attentive to the needs of others and act with love, knowing that God sees and values every act of kindness.
